sentences.text: 10.Per contra, the learned Special Government appearing on behalf of the respondents 1 and 2 in both petitions and the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the National Highways Authority of India/third respondent in both petitions submitted that there is no question of directing the first respondent to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD)Nos.11952 & 12002 of 2020 once again determine the compensation, since the first respondent had already passed an award and he has become functus officio.
If the petitioners were aggrieved by the award passed by the first respondent, they ought to have challenged the same under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
It was therefore, contended that the relief sought for by the petitioner is unsustainable.

11.It was further submitted that the first respondent has remanded the matter back to the file of the second respondent only with the direction to the second respondent to fix the compensation in line with the award that was passed by the first respondent.

This direction given by the first respondent cannot be expanded and the petitioners cannot be allowed to seek for redetermination of the compensation and therefore, it was contended that the petitioners are attempting to reopen the award, which has already become final.
In view of the same, they urged this Court to dismiss these writ petitions.

12.The issue that arises for consideration in both writ petitions is as to whether this Court must direct the first respondent to deal with the application that was filed by the petitioners in line with Section 3(G)(5) of the Act.

and passed an award.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners had filed the arbitration application before the first respondent /arbitrator under Section 3(G) (5) of the Act.

This arbitration application was considered by the first respondent/arbitrator and the first respondent through proceedings dated 18.09.2016 and 14.08.2016, respectively had directed the second respondent to provide the appropriate compensation to the land owners, based on the present guideline value after determining the same from the valuable sources and thereby, to take care of the interest of the land owners.
14.On a careful reading of this order, it is seen that the first respondent has already passed the award in this case and the first respondent had remitted the matter back to the file of the competent authority only for the recalculation of the same in line with the award passed by the first respondent /arbitrator.

The second respondent /competent authority on receipt of the same, has calculated the compensation by taking the guideline value as on 01.04.2012 and has come to the conclusion that the petitioner in W.P. (MD)No.11952 of 2020 has to be paid a total compensation of Rs.3,80,572/-
and the petitioner in W.P.(MD)No.12002 of 2020 must be paid with the total compensation of Rs.1,65,277/-.

4 15.The limited scope that is available to the petitioners is to see as to whether the compensation that was fixed by the second respondent/competent authority is in line with the award that was passed by the first respondent/arbitrator.

According to the petitioners, the first respondent/arbitrator while passing the award in the year 2016 had mentioned in the award that proper compensation must be fixed based on the present guideline value.

Whereas, the competent authority has fixed the compensation based on the guideline value as on 01.04.2012.
16.Whether

this recalculation of the compensation amount by the competent authority is in accordance with the award of the District Collector /arbitrator can be the only issue, which can be gone into in this case.

That is the reason why the first respondent /arbitrator on receipt of the applications from the petitioners, directed the second respondent /competent authority to take appropriate action and to inform the same to the first respondent.

The directions issued by the first respondent cannot be found fault with, since there was no occasion for the first respondent to once again go through the process of arbitration as he had become functus officio and at the best, the first respondent can only ask the second respondent/competent authority as to whether the award passed by the first respondent has been properly understood and complied with while recalculating the compensation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD)Nos.11952 & 12002 of 2020 amount that is payable to the petitioners.
17.This is exactly the information that the first respondent has sought for from the second respondent /competent authority through proceedings dated 21.10.2017.
In view of the same, there is no scope for interfering with the proceedings of the first respondent dated 21.10.2017 in both these writ petitions.

18.The petitioners in the guise of seeking for redetermination of compensation, are attempting to go into certain other issues like determination of compensation under the 2013 Act and those are issues, which are beyond the scope of determination as on date.

In other words, the petitioners cannot be allowed to reopen the arbitration proceedings, which has already come to an end and by coming up with certain new issues, it cannot once again be gone into by the first respondent/arbitrator.
19.In light of the above discussion, there shall be a direction to the second respondent /competent authority to act upon the proceedings of the first respondent/arbitrator dated 21.10.2017.

The second respondent shall correctly understand the purport of the award that was passed by the first respondent /arbitrator through proceedings dated 18.09.2016 and 14.08.2016,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.(MD)Nos.11952 & 12002 of 2020 respectively and pass appropriate orders.

To make it more clearer, the second respondent /competent authority shall once again look into the issue as to whether the compensation was properly recalculated and whether any rectification /correction is required on the compensation that was already determined by the second respondent through proceedings dated 14.11.2016 and Nil.10.2016, respectively.

20.If ultimately the second respondent /competent authority comes to the conclusion that the compensation that was determined through the above proceedings is not correct and in line with the award passed by the District Collector /arbitrator, the correct compensation amount shall be Michael Mathura Sing vs The Arbitrator Under The National ... on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60517734/
